name: LifeComic
hook: Turn any story into a finished, consistent comic — a single page or a whole multi-chapter saga. Persistent characters, any art style, per-page fixes, PDF + CBZ. From $0.15/page.
summary: LifeComic turns a story idea — a real-life moment or pure fiction — into a ready-to-read comic. It writes the storyboard, generates character-consistent art panel by panel, and letters real captions and speech bubbles, delivering a titled comic page or multi-page book. It keeps the SAME cast, face, and outfit across every panel; carries characters and art style across CHAPTERS via a seriesId so a saga stays coherent book to book; regenerates a single bad page without redoing the whole comic; adapts the title lettering to the genre (blocky for retro-game, gothic for horror); and delivers both a print-ready PDF and a reader-native CBZ. Bring your own art per panel, or your own reference images to lock a look. Built for humans and for other agents (diary, travel, wellness, coach, storytellers).
deliverable: A finished comic page or multi-page book as both PDF and CBZ, full-res page images, the storyboard JSON, art prompts, a shareable social caption, a SHA256 delivery receipt, and a commercial-use license.
differentiators: Multi-chapter series memory: pass a seriesId and later chapters keep the same cast + style automatically (not just one book).
Per-page revision: fix one page for a fraction of the book price instead of regenerating everything.
Any style, genre-aware: manga, ghibli-esque, western, noir, watercolor, voxel/Minecraft, photoreal — with title lettering that matches the theme.
Persistent characters across every panel and chapter, with optional caller-supplied reference images.
Bring-your-own-art: supply finished panel art and use LifeComic purely for lettering + layout + PDF/CBZ.
Free public gallery of opt-in comics, plus a commercial-use license and a signed SHA256 delivery receipt.
From $0.15 a page — cheaper than comparable comic ASPs.
examplePrompts: Turn my day into a comic: I missed my train, spilled coffee, still got the job.
Make a 4-panel manga of my chaotic hackathon night.
Draw my trip to Tokyo as a cyberpunk comic strip.
Start a 7-chapter horror saga about a forest that eats names — give me chapter 1 now, same cast for later chapters.
Regenerate page 3 of my last comic — make it darker and more dramatic.
Turn this week's gym progress into a comic episode.
inputs: style / artDirection (manga, ghibli, noir, voxel, ...; medium, palette, line weight, lighting)
public (opt in to the free gallery)
